name: Monolaurin (glycerol monolaurate) vaginal gel
short: Vaginal gel: two thirds of women had mild-to-moderate urogenital adverse events, as often as with placebo (109 women). Pregnant and breastfeeding women excluded; no data on use by mouth.
text: This entry covers monolaurin gel put in the vagina. In a double-blind randomised trial of 5% monolaurin vaginal gel against a placebo gel in 109 women with bacterial vaginosis, two thirds of both groups reported solicited urogenital adverse events, which were mild to moderate and did not differ significantly between groups (p = .24); pregnant and breastfeeding women were not included. In a randomised double-blind study of 36 women colonised or infected with Candida or Gardnerella vaginalis, no adverse events were reported with monolaurin vaginal gels used for 2 days. By mouth: a 2019 review found no peer-reviewed evidence for clinical use of monolaurin as a dietary supplement, and found only 3 peer-reviewed papers showing antimicrobial effects of monolaurin in people, all for use in the vagina or mouth; the cited sources give no adverse-event data for monolaurin taken by mouth. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
